blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content: Continuous particle systems are an important subject of investigation in rigorous statistical mechanics. Since the thirties it was clear that the equation of state of a non ideal gas in thermodynamics can be deduced from statistical mechanics via the Mayer series of the pressure in the grand canonical ensemble. The Mayer series, proposed by Mayer (see, e.g., [@MM] and references therein) is an expansion in powers of the fugacity $\l$ of the logarithm of the Grand Canonical partition function of the the system under study, whose $n^{\rm th}$-order coefficient is given by a sum of terms indexed

Convergence of Mayer and Virial expansions and the Penrose tree-graph
identity
Aldo Procacci∗, Sergio A. Yuhjtman†
November 8, 2018
Abstract
We establish new lower bounds for the convergence radius of the Mayer series and the
Virial series of a continuous particle system interacting via a stable and tempered pair
potential. Our bounds considerably improve those given by Penrose and Ruelle in 1963 for
the Mayer series and by Lebowitz and Penrose in 1964 for the Virial series. To get our results
we exploit the tree-graph identity given by Penrose in 1967

blocks.title: Comparison with recent results and concluding remarks
blocks.content: As observed in Section 2, the improvement of Theorem [\[teo1\]](#teo1){reference-type="ref" reference="teo1"} respect to the old Penrose-Ruelle bound is manifestly evident, as far as general stable and tempered pair potentials are concerned. There have been however recent works [@MPS; @dLP; @dLPY] which also obtain improvements on the convergence radius of the Mayer series for systems of particles interacting via a restricted class of stable and tempered pair potentials.
